claims.claim: Docs drift when code or product behavior changes without a docs update
claims.quote: Documentation drifts when code or product behavior changes without a corresponding content update.

claims.claim: Code review can pass while a tutorial still uses a renamed API parameter; no build failure results
UI renames pass acceptance tests while screenshots and instructions stay outdated
Deprecated endpoints stay documented; examples break once endpoint removed
More frequent releases increase chances of divergence
claims.quote: Frequent releases increase the number of opportunities for divergence.

claims.claim: Each docs area should have a named technical owner; API owner accountable for API accuracy
Ownership wikis go stale because changing a service owner does not update the release workflow
claims.quote: A separate ownership wiki often becomes stale

claims.claim: One named owner should approve technical accuracy; shared responsibility lets omissions be deferred
Each docs area needs a primary owner and a defined substitute
Each PR needs a docs impact decision: link update, open tracked task with owner and deadline, or explain no effect
CI can block merging when docs field empty, linked task lacks owner, or required update missing
Emergency releases may bypass gate but must create follow-up task with owner and due date
Release gates enforce participation but cannot prove docs are correct
claims.quote: Release gates enforce participation, but they cannot prove that the docs are correct.

claims.claim: GitBook Git Sync plus change requests give technical and non-technical contributors one review path
Same gate can be implemented with another repo and CI system
Prose review can leave incorrect endpoint or permission rule untouched; source validation checks claims against code/spec/product
Must define which source wins when docs and spec conflict
Sample live user journeys in a clean environment; auth, billing, destructive ops need closer checks
Automated checks need a defined source and failure condition; 'check the docs' is too vague for CI
Content Gaps compares questions and connected records with docs, flags missing/outdated/incorrect content ranked by severity
Content Gaps adds a daily signal
Reviewers ask GitBook Agent to draft a change request; a person still verifies governing source before merge
Page age does not determine correctness
claims.quote: Page age does not determine correctness.

claims.claim: Freshness checks need last-reviewed date, owner, review interval
Stable conceptual pages may need annual review; deployment/auth instructions every release cycle
Mapping docs areas to repos/directories and flagging pages when code changes is a stronger signal than page age
Code-change flag creates a review task, not a declaration of inaccuracy
Avoid auto-publishing a stale label unless page age reliably indicates a problem for readers
Each supported version needs own docs scope, owner, and freshness checks; archive old versions rather than delete
Version history and content variants solve different problems
Broken Links flags inbound links to docs pages returning 404; does not crawl every internal or external link
Current Quality checks are an early step toward broader automated validation, not a complete suite
GitBook Agent and MCP cannot decide whether an undocumented code change is intended or unfinished
Automated repair creates reviewable change rather than publishing instantly
Named reviewer must approve every change affecting documented behavior
Pre-release checklist has 14 items
Automated validation cannot determine product intent or confirm every technical claim

analysis_rows.symptom: Tutorial uses old API parameter name after rename
analysis_rows.cause: Code review verifies code, release workflow does not connect docs artifact
analysis_rows.fix: link docs update to PR; docs impact decision; CI check

analysis_rows.symptom: Screenshots and instructions describe previous UI
analysis_rows.cause: Button rename or moved setting passes acceptance tests without docs change
analysis_rows.fix: repeat documented flow in release candidate; product owner review

analysis_rows.symptom: Examples keep sending new users to deprecated endpoint, then break at removal
analysis_rows.cause: Nothing requires docs change when deprecation begins
analysis_rows.fix: update trigger on endpoint change; compare docs to spec and tests

analysis_rows.cause: Changing a service owner does not update release workflow
analysis_rows.fix: keep ownership in repo ownership rules, PR templates, product tickets

analysis_rows.cause: Shared responsibility without a final approver
analysis_rows.fix: one named owner approves technical accuracy; backup owner

analysis_rows.symptom: Passing release gate but docs still wrong
analysis_rows.cause: Gate confirms a page was edited, not that instructions match product
analysis_rows.fix: reviewers inspect docs diff alongside code change

analysis_rows.symptom: Recently edited page conflicts with release, or old page still accurate
analysis_rows.fix: source comparison plus freshness checks plus code-change flags

analysis_rows.symptom: Automation cannot decide if undocumented code change is intended
analysis_rows.fix: product owner or engineer resolves ambiguity
